fatal_errors: The proposed Mo-to-V substitution does not reconstruct the targeted 4.2 at.% Cr addition and associated reticulated Laves-phase intervention.
No specific Mo substitution fraction is selected, so the purported single intervention is not compositionally well defined.
The cited evidence supports low-density alloying only in general and does not show that replacing Mo with V in HfMoTaTiZr will retain approximately 800 MPa yield strength at 1000 °C.
The falsification rule omits an elevated-temperature strength threshold despite preservation of high-temperature performance being central to the hypothesis.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the density/performance trade-off and proposes a controllable alloying experiment, so it is a plausible alternative rather than wholly unsupported. However, it misses the target intervention, secondary-phase morphology, lattice contraction, and dual strengthening/toughening mechanism. Its generic BCC solid-solution explanation does not address how ductility or crack resistance would be preserved. The experiment includes controls and numerical rejection thresholds, but varying unspecified substitution ratios is not a single defined intervention, fracture toughness lacks a quantitative criterion, and no rejection criterion tests the claimed 1000 °C performance. The cited papers establish that lighter refractory additions can reduce density, but they do not validate the specific Mo-to-V substitution or the proposed strength values.
